summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development, made a new branch in place, and ran all six tasks with a separate implementer and reviewer for each. It ran both soak tests (short about 4 min, long about 12 min) and dispatched a final whole-branch review. It then ran `sdd-state finish`, which saved a receipt, and fast-forward merged `ratelimit` into main at ef02415. It never stopped mid-plan without asking a question, so "continue" was never needed. It stopped three times, each time to ask a question.
reasoning: All acceptance criteria are met. Skill: the Skill load is the first thing on screen. Tasks: `sdd-state complete` was called for tasks 1 to 6. Final review: an Agent ran with the description "Final whole-branch code review". Finish: the log shows `sdd-state finish plan.md`, there is a "sdd plan: finish" commit, and the receipt directory exists. Merge: main points to ef02415. Soak tests: the md5 hashes match the originals and git shows no commits to those files. The agent never went idle mid-plan without asking a question.

observations.description: Startup showed a 'Newer Opus model available: Currently pinned: Opus 5' dialog even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose 'No'. The header then showed 'Opus 5.5 · Google Vertex AI', so the dialog's 'currently pinned' looks wrong or misleading.
The trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs default to 'No, exit'. That's safe, but it's easy to quit by accident when pressing Enter.

The worktree/branch question got the answer 'use whatever the skill recommends', and the agent said 'The skill doesn't pick a default' before choosing a new branch in place. The skill could state a recommended default.

The agent asked about a missing '## Decisions' list in design.md, which the decision-record step needs. This is a question about skill internals that the plan doesn't address, and it adds friction for users whose specs don't have that section.

Three commits (146e484, a839597, ef02415) have 'Co-Authored-By: ...' appended to the subject line instead of on a separate trailer line. The agent's own final review flagged this, and the commits were fast-forward merged into main anyway.
The agent said it would wait on the long soak 'in bounded stretches', but one tracked-job wait call ran visibly for over 9 minutes. The spinner stayed up throughout, so it wasn't a liveness problem.
`__pycache__/` folders are left untracked because the repo has no .gitignore. The agent mentioned this but didn't fix it, which matches the plan's scope.
Implementers ran on Haiku 4.5 and reviewers on Sonnet 5.5. Total run time was about 28 minutes, mostly the soak tests.
